title: Ticked the AI boxes on itch and expected my idle game to sink. It made New & Popular the next day (barely)
author: Juridiwy
selftext:
Lots of posts here lately about getting burned for being upfront about AI, so I figured I'd share one that went the other way, at least a bit.

I made [Everything is a Mimic!](https://talemonger.itch.io/everything-is-a-mimic), a free browser idle game where you're a treasure chest that eats adventurers. Their gold wakes up the rest of the furniture, then the stuff outside, and eventually the Moon. Once you've eaten enough, a Hero comes to slay you, so you flee to a new shell and keep a permanent gold bonus. That's the prestige.

Claude wrote all of the code and the in-game text. I ticked the AI boxes on itch for code and text (not graphics or sound), so the page has the "AI Assisted" label, and I was pretty sure that would sink it.

It went public on 9 Nov, and by the next afternoon it was on New & Popular: #21 for incremental, #21 for idle, and dead last (#36) on the first page of web games. Never the main page, and the numbers are small. Right now it's 264 views, 201 browser plays, 4.7k impressions at 3.2% CTR, and 46 people who opted in to anonymous stats. Every referral so far came from itch itself, since I hadn't posted it anywhere. Zero ratings, zero comments.

No idea which of these actually mattered, but this is what I did:

- No image generators at all. I had Claude mock up the same scene four ways, picked the cartoon one, and every object is drawn in canvas code. Each mimic got its own face. The door's welcome mat is its tongue, and the statue's eyes follow whoever walks past. There's a gallery page with every object in every pose, so I can check the art without playing.

- The game rules live in one file with no browser code, so a bot can play it headless in four styles (busy clicker down to mostly idle) and spit out a pacing table. About 100 checks run before every upload.

- Opt-in stats from day one. The first night they showed that only 3 of 9 players ever saw the first Hero, because it took ~16 min of busy clicking. Next morning I moved it to ~5 min and made the first Hero miss on purpose, so you learn the timing for free. Since then 22 of 36 have reached it.

- Lots of small updates. Five went out in the first day.

- Phones. itch's frame is tiny on a phone held sideways. I tested on my iPhone and my son's Samsung, and two of those five updates were just phone layout fixes.

- Mechanics came from playing it, not from a plan. I left it open in another window for 33 minutes and completely broke the economy, so now the Hero has a countdown and can actually catch you. Wait past the countdown and you get a Daring bonus, so every prestige is a bit of a gamble.

What I'm watching now is whether anyone comes back the next day. Too early to tell.

comments.author: Bonelessgummybear
comments.body: Referencing a meme is a smart name move. I knew it sounded familiar when I read the title

replies.author: Advice2Anyone
replies.body: The how come my where is John Cena books are not flying off the shelves

comments.author: clydeagain
comments.body: Pretty fun but the screen shake every single click gets dizzying

replies.author: clydeagain
replies.body: I wanted to keep playing but couldn't stand the vibration, I think a vibration effect that strong should be reserved for another source of sgrong impact every once a while, also didn't think wobble on/off did anything or didn't understand what it did

replies.author: Juridiwy
replies.body: Thanks for the details! I think I'll be able to update the game once more before going to bed, so the vibration will be gone/reduced in 1-2 hours.

replies.author: Juridiwy
replies.body: Update in case you come back: biting doesn't shake the screen anymore, only the big moments do (like the Hero's swing), and it fades out fast. Also renamed Wobble to "Motion", and turning it off now kills the shake completely.

comments.author: MintL1
comments.body:
It was fun but on my android phone the labels above the menu would change width depending on the digits in the money label forcing the other labels to wrap to a new row and making the menu constantly go and up down. 

Also I noticed that when I pressed on a label it tried to open Google search.

replies.author: Juridiwy
replies.body:
Thanks for playing the game, and for the feedback!   
  
Both issues should be fixed now: the boxes above the menu have now fixed sizes, so nothing moves when the numbers change, and text can't be selected anymore, which is what was triggering the Google search. Lmk if you ever give it another try

comments.author: thewalkingcity
comments.body: The Idle games audience doesn't seem to mind AI content as much as other genres. I have released a few on itch and only had 1 or 2 comments out of thousands of hours played.
